issues.issue: Do Canada's international law obligations (Protocol I) require excluding from paragraph 34(1)(b) force used for self-determination?
issues.applicant_position: Protocol I makes force for self-determination legitimate, so it is not "subversion by force"; Division should have applied international law.
issues.respondent_position: Clear wording of s.34(1)(b) covers any government; legitimacy of force is for the Minister's exemption, and international law does not require exclusion.
issues.result_quote: I would answer the certified question, as formulated by the judge or reformulated at paragraph 46, in the negative.

issues.issue: Must paragraph 34(1)(f) be read down under section 2(d) of the Charter to exclude lawful Canadian organizations such as the KDPI?
issues.applicant_position: Charter freedom of association requires reading down 34(1)(f) to exclude organizations lawful in Canada without illegal activity abroad.
issues.respondent_position: Charter not engaged, as only legislated benefits are removed; relies on Suresh that s.2(d) does not protect membership in violent organizations.
issues.result_quote: I conclude that the Division could not reasonably construe the word “organization” as excluding an organization operating in Canada
